ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The applicant must implement a risk-based screening program covering all UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories and material counterparties against the UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, EU/UK/HK sanctions lists, PRC anti-money laundering and untrustworthy persons lists, PBOC risk lists, INTERPOL Red Notices, global regulatory enforcement databases and adverse media. PEPs and their family members or close associates require enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth and source of funds documentation, senior management approval, and enhanced transaction monitoring. Any sanctions hit must be immediately escalated to legal and compliance; unusual transaction reports must be filed with the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center (CAMLMAC) as required. Screening results and underlying records must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE name must be registered in standard simplified Chinese characters in the four-tier statutory structure: administrative division plus trade name plus industry or business description plus legal form, e.g. administrative district name, trade name, industry description, and "Co., Ltd.". Pinyin or English transliteration may be registered as a supplementary name but cannot replace the Chinese statutory name. For a Taiwan investor, the simplified Chinese transliteration of the investor name is preferred; traditional Chinese forms must be converted to simplified Chinese for SAMR filing, and the English trade name must be phonetically consistent with the Chinese name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: After a name rejection, the applicant must first obtain a written rejection notice identifying the conflicting token or rule. The applicant or entrusted formation agent may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the SAMR office one level above the rejecting bureau within 60 days of receipt, attaching the rejection notice, proposed name, lease or address evidence, investor passport and board resolution. The higher SAMR must decide within 60 days. If the reconsideration fails, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within 6 months. Two or three backup names should be submitted for simultaneous preliminary clearance to preserve pipeline speed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected for this WFOE and for the remote BPO call-center industry. PRC Company Law requires a fixed and identifiable business address for the registered office; tax registration, invoice issuance, corporate bank account opening and SAMR on-site inspection all require physical business premises. A call-center BPO must demonstrate actual workstations, IP telephony infrastructure, data processing controls, employee social insurance rolls and business records at the registered address. Banks will refuse account opening where the address is only a virtual mailbox. A serviced or co-working office is acceptable only if it has an exclusive suite number, a substantive lease agreement, rent receipts and physical signage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: lease agreement and rental receipts, utility bills, physical signage matching the registered name, workstations and telephony equipment, call-center shift logs, employee social insurance payment rolls, data processing and information security system logs, internal control records, and business books at the registered address. Quantified risk: Low-to-Moderate, with approximately 25% to 35% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the municipal tax authority or SAMR for a foreign-controlled WFOE in a labor-intensive BPO operation. The probability increases if the registered address is inconsistent with the actual place of business, if remote work sites are not disclosed, or if tax filing metrics show anomalies. SAMR may also conduct random double-random one-open inspections, making address consistency and documentary readiness mandatory.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 Revision), Articles 23-30 (Incorporation), 37-40 (Shareholders' Meeting), 46-49 (Board of Directors), and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 4-6, 12-14
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – Local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (e.g., Shanghai Municipal Administration for Market Regulation)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise (Form F-1) together with the Articles of Association and the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the Foreign Investment Law; however, the registered capital must be fully subscribed and paid within the period specified in the Articles of Association (typically 30 years). No escrow or blocked account requirement is imposed by law, but the capital must be remitted into a designated foreign exchange account in accordance with SAFE regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (THE 'COMPANY') ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE]. WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the laws of the People's Republic of China as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) with limited liability; and WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to take all actions necessary to commence business operations and to comply with all statutory requirements. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription of the entire registered capital of the Company, amounting to [USD 100,000] (or its equivalent in RMB), by the sole shareholder, [Parent Company Name], as set forth in the Articles of Association. The Board directs the Chief Financial Officer to open a foreign exchange capital account with a licensed bank in China and to ensure that the subscribed capital is remitted in accordance with the capital contribution schedule. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name], including a basic deposit account, a general deposit account, and a foreign exchange settlement account. The Board designates the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer as joint signatories for all banking transactions, with the authority to execute any agreements, mandates, and instructions necessary for the operation of such accounts. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [Address], which shall be the legal seat of the Company for all statutory and administrative purposes. The Board directs the Company Secretary to file the registered office address with the Market Supervision Administration and to ensure that all corporate records and seals are maintained at this location. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints [Name] as the General Manager, [Name] as the Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as the Company Secretary, each to serve until their successors are duly elected or appointed. The Board authorizes the General Manager to represent the Company in all matters, including the execution of contracts, the hiring of employees, and the conduct of day-to-day operations, subject to the limitations set forth in the Articles of Association. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes any officer of the Company to execute and deliver all documents, certificates, and instruments, and to take all such actions as may be necessary or advisable to implement the foregoing resolutions, including the preparation and filing of all statutory returns and the procurement of any required licenses. This resolution shall be effective immediately and shall remain in full force and effect until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have executed this resolution as of the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) – Online via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for name pre-approval through the SAMR online portal. The application must include the proposed company name in Chinese (e.g., '上海[Company Name]有限公司'), the intended business scope (ISIC 7820 – temporary employment agency services, but for BPO call center, we will specify 'customer service outsourcing, telemarketing, and remote helpdesk services'), and the legal form (WFOE). The authority will verify that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered entities and that the business scope complies with the Foreign Investment Negative List. If the name is approved, a Name Pre-Approval Certificate is issued, valid for 6 months. This step is mandatory before filing the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in Chinese and English
Identification documents of the foreign investor (passport or corporate certificate)
Power of attorney for the local agent (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity or non-compliance, the applicant may file a new name application with a revised name or submit an appeal to the SAMR within 15 days, providing evidence of distinctiveness or prior use.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Documents to SAMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) – Enterprise Registration Window or Online via the National Enterprise Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name pre-approval, prepare and submit the full incorporation dossier to the SAMR. The dossier must include the signed Articles of Association, the lease agreement for the registered office, the identity documents of the directors and legal representative, and the capital contribution schedule. The application must be filed on the prescribed Form F-1. The SAMR will review the documents for legal compliance, including the business scope, capital structure, and governance provisions. If all requirements are met, the SAMR will issue the Business License (营业执照) within the statutory period. The license serves as the certificate of incorporation and includes the unified social credit code.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association (signed by all shareholders)
Lease agreement for registered office (with property ownership certificate)
Identity certificates of directors, legal representative, and supervisors
Capital contribution schedule and proof of investor qualification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, the applicant must respond to the SAMR's written notice within 15 days, providing additional clarifications or corrections. If the issue is not resolved, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the higher-level SAMR or initiate an administrative lawsuit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations (Tax, Social Insurance, and Statistics)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) – Local Tax Bureau; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (MOHRSS) – Local Social Insurance Bureau; National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) – Local Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of obtaining the Business License, the company must complete tax registration with the local tax bureau, obtaining a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and registering for value-added tax (VAT) and corporate income tax (CIT). Simultaneously, the company must register with the social insurance bureau for employee social security contributions and with the statistics bureau for statistical reporting. The company must also open a social insurance contribution account and a housing fund account. These registrations are mandatory for legal operation and to avoid penalties. The process can be completed online through the integrated government service platform.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening certificate (if already opened)
Employee list and social insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any registration is delayed or rejected, the company may submit a written explanation and supporting documents to the respective authority. For tax registration, the company can apply for an extension of up to 30 days. If the issue persists, the company may seek assistance from the local investment promotion agency or a licensed tax consultant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Banks Licensed by the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business License and tax registration, the company must open a basic deposit account with a commercial bank. The bank will require the Business License, the Articles of Association, the legal representative's identity, and the company seal. The bank will also open a foreign exchange capital account for the receipt of the foreign investor's capital contribution. The capital must be remitted from the foreign shareholder's account and converted into RMB at the prevailing exchange rate. The bank will report the capital inflow to SAFE through the Foreign Exchange Registration System. The company must ensure that the capital is used in accordance with the approved business scope and that the capital contribution is verified by a certified public accountant within 6 months of the remittance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete documents, the company must rectify the deficiencies and resubmit. If the capital remittance is delayed or blocked by SAFE, the company must provide additional documentation, such as the capital contribution schedule and the source of funds, and may apply for a one-time extension.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); taxpayer-facing online services are delivered through the National Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) platform at the official STA portal (www.chinatax.gov.cn) and the local electronic tax bureaux.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor establishing a PRC wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) must first apply for a Foreign-Invested Enterprise business licence at the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under the Foreign Investment Law. The licence carries a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which automatically becomes the taxpayer identification number for all PRC national tax, local tax, social insurance and VAT purposes; no separate TIN is issued. The SAMR registration data is synchronised to the competent local office of the State Taxation Administration, completing the statutory tax registration without a separate application. The WFOE must then complete supplementary VAT onboarding in the e-Tax platform: select the VAT taxpayer status (general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer), apply for invoice allotment in the National VAT Invoice System, configure the electronic invoice/digital invoice module, and appoint a tax representative/accounting entity. If a foreign non-resident enterprise itself has a taxable presence or engages in cross-border supply without incorporation, it must complete a non-resident tax registration at the local STA, obtain a temporary taxpayer code for withholding purposes, and file China-source income tax and VAT through the withholding agent mechanism.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification: the WFOE is automatically treated as a PRC resident enterprise taxed at entity level; no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under PRC tax law. For VAT purposes, the WFOE may elect between small-scale taxpayer treatment and general taxpayer treatment subject to the RMB 5 million annual turnover threshold, and may elect to apply VAT zero-rating rather than exemption for eligible cross-border services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no monetary turnover threshold for basic tax registration because the WFOE is registered at incorporation. The mandatory turnover threshold for VAT general taxpayer registration is RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales; below that, the small-scale VAT taxpayer rate applies. The remote BPO call-centre and tele-sales service, as a modern service, is normally chargeable at 6% VAT domestically and at 0% when qualifying as an exported service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The PRC uses a nationwide VAT invoice management system (the National VAT Invoice System). All special VAT invoices and digital e-invoices are issued through the taxpayer's authorised invoicing software or the fully digitalised electronic invoice (digital e-invoice) platform and are uploaded in real time to the State Taxation Administration's central data warehouse for automated cross-matching, anomaly detection and anti-fraud analysis. Invoice numbers are centrally allocated by the tax authority; digital invoices carry cryptographic verification codes and electronic signatures (anti-fraud digital stamping). There is no public third-party fiscal-clearance API comparable to Latin American electronic invoicing; instead, qualified taxpayers integrate with the official e-Tax/e-invoice service interfaces for invoice issuance, red-letter reversal, input VAT certification, and export rebate filing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the PRC VAT cross-border taxable conduct rules (the VAT pilot programme and its cross-border supply annex, as amended), a PRC VAT general taxpayer supplying business-process-management services, including call centre operations, inbound helpdesk and outbound tele-sales BPO, to an overseas recipient located in Taiwan (jurisdiction TW) may apply the 0% VAT rate if the services are completely consumed outside the PRC, the recipient is not a PRC unit or individual, the service is supplied under a written contract, and the export consideration is received in foreign currency and repatriated to the PRC. The export service must be recorded as zero-rated sales in the VAT return, and the taxpayer must retain documented evidence supporting offshore consumption, including client tax-status evidence, service delivery records, call logs and payment flows. If the service is provided to a PRC-related party's Taiwan establishment or is partially consumed in China, zero-rating is denied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) - required where physical goods or ancillary equipment are exported from the PRC customs territory
Bill of Lading, air waybill or equivalent transport document - required for physical export movements; not applicable to pure remote BPO call-centre services
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher evidencing receipt and repatriation of the export consideration in foreign currency from Taiwan
Cross-border service contract, statement of work or purchase order identifying the Taiwan recipient and the offshore service scope

Evidence of offshore consumption: customer tax/corporate registration certificate, service delivery records, call detail records, and telephony/IP-based delivery logs demonstrating no PRC taxable consumption
PRC VAT zero-rated/special invoice issued through the e-invoice system or invoice management platform
Foreign exchange settlement and declaration records from the designated bank, including the export proceeds repatriation monitoring record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may conduct post-export audit and require production of the full substantiation file. If zero-rating is improperly claimed, the tax authority will claw back the zero-rated output VAT, deny or recover input VAT refunds, exact late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and impose an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid VAT under the Tax Administration Law of the PRC. Fraudulent export or circular transactions are additionally subject to inclusion in the abnormal taxpayer list, tightening of invoice allotment, export rebate suspension, and criminal liability for tax fraud under the Criminal Law of the PRC if the amounts or intent meet statutory thresholds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China maintains a managed floating exchange rate regime with RMB convertibility restricted on the capital account while substantially liberalized on the current account. The Chinese WFOE can freely settle legitimate service-export revenues and pay current-account operating expenses through designated banks, but every cross-border transaction must be supported by genuine commercial documents and reflected in the SAFE foreign exchange monitoring system. On the capital side, FDI equity injection from the Taiwan parent requires approval or filing with the Ministry of Commerce and SAFE; once remitted, funds are credited to a foreign-currency capital account and can be settled into RMB for qualifying use only after presenting a capital verification report and a payment-purpose application. Profit remittances to Taiwan are permitted after audited financials, corporate income tax settlement, and board declaration are completed, but are treated as capital-account dividend remittances and must be routed through a Chinese bank with the correct purpose code. A WFOE cannot freely convert CNY into foreign currency for cross-border lending or overseas investments without prior SAFE registration; hence treasury planning must pre-approve each major flow. The RMB is not fully convertible offshore, and the Taiwan parent should expect settlement lags and documentary scrutiny.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's trade-monitoring scheme, the WFOE must collect export and service proceeds through a domestic designated foreign-exchange bank and match the incoming funds to underlying contracts and invoices in the SAFE foreign exchange monitoring system. Repatriation should generally occur within 180 days of the service performance date unless SAFE has approved a later collection. There is no fixed percentage surrender obligation; once received, the enterprise may retain the foreign currency in its current-account foreign-exchange account or voluntarily convert into RMB, but the retained funds may only be used for genuine operating needs. Delayed collection, partial write-offs, or settlement through third-party accounts require prior notification or filing to the local SAFE branch and must be supported by the client contract, service invoice, completion report, and a statement of non-offshore retention.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable for the mainland WFOE. Wise B2B is not a deposit-taking bank or licensed payment institution under PRC law and cannot settle RMB through CIPS or provide SAFE-compliant trade background vetting for an onshore Chinese entity. The Taiwan parent may use Wise only for low-value ancillary remittances to the WFOE's Chinese bank account, but Wise must not be used as an account provider or clearing rail for the WFOE's CNY treasury. All onshore accounts must be held at a SAFE-designated domestic commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in-branch physical presence is required for account opening by either the registered legal representative or an authorised account handler holding a notarised and legalised power of attorney. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by Chinese banks as the sole onboarding method; a live compliance interview, original company chops, passport or ID verification, and issuance of a bank seal card are mandatory. If the statutory director resides in Taiwan, the WFOE should appoint a mainland finance manager as the account handler and still expect a video call with the ultimate beneficial owner during the compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity because the Taiwan parent holds the WFOE through a discretionary trust or an investment holding company with multiple layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and registry extract for every trust and holding-company layer; trust deed and formal trustee letter; passports or identity documents of all natural-person beneficiaries; ownership chart demonstrating all individuals holding a 25% or greater economic or voting interest; audited financial statements and tax returns of the Taiwan parent for the last two years; bank reference letter from the Taiwanese remitting bank confirming the source of foreign-currency funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: One lump-sum USD capital injection into a newly incorporated WFOE with no operating history and before the final business license and SAFE registration are fully completed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment approval or filing receipt from MOFCOM; final business license; articles of association; board resolution approving the capital contribution schedule; source-of-wealth statement for the Taiwanese shareholder, comprising audited financials, corporate dividend records, employment income proof, or sale-of-assets documentation; original bank statement showing funds originated from the Taiwan parent's designated bank account; signed undertaking confirming no nominee arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-amount inbound cross-border service payments from many unrelated overseas clients, creating structuring or trade-based money-laundering red flags for a remote BPO call-center operation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with each client showing pricing methodology; detailed commercial invoices matching each individual receipt; call-center operating evidence including CRM logs, telephony records, agent rosters, and work schedules; payroll registries proving actual personnel are employed in the Chinese WFOE; corporate income tax and VAT filings corroborating declared revenue; a narrative explanation of the remote BPO value chain and a clear mapping of each remitter to a contracted client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Treasury operations involving rapid back-to-back CNY-to-foreign-currency conversions or same-day settlement to offshore accounts, possibly indicating round-tripping or underground foreign-exchange activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved cash-flow projection and monthly treasury calendar; underlying invoices and purchase orders for each conversion; SAFE trade-monitoring system report screens displaying transaction background; external debt registration certificate and loan agreement if the conversion relates to shareholder loans; written confirmation that no RMB amounts are converted to USD for overseas investments without prior SAFE approval; and a statement of no third-party lending or foreign-exchange speculation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must remit investment capital via SWIFT MT103 from a Taiwan regulated bank to the WFOE's Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a Chinese designated bank such as Bank of China. The remittance message should include the SAFE-compliant foreign direct investment purpose code for equity injection, together with the MOFCOM filing certificate, articles of association, and board resolution. After receipt, the bank issues a capital-entry voucher, a PRC registered accountant performs capital verification, and the SAFE FDI system records the shareholder equity registration. Any subsequent conversion from USD to RMB must be supported by a capital-account use form and may only be applied to permitted business purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic operating disbursements for salaries, rent, and telecom are paid in RMB through the WFOE's corporate online banking platform and CIPS for any cross-border RMB elements. Cross-border service purchases from Taiwan or other jurisdictions are settled by open-account SWIFT MT103 using the relevant SAFE current-account purpose code, underlying service contract, invoice, and proof of actual service delivery. For physical imports such as telephony hardware or IT equipment, the WFOE may use commercial irrevocable letters of credit or documentary collections (D/P or D/A) through the issuing Chinese bank, supported by customs declarations, shipping documents, and inspection certificates. The WFOE should prefer cross-border RMB settlement under CIPS to reduce FX conversion risk and processing time.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a licensed Chinese bank for genuine current-account trade and service-flow exposures, requiring underlying documentation and prohibition of speculative positions.
Foreign exchange swaps between CNY and USD or TWD limited to matching the timing of documented receipts and payments without exceeding the notional amount of the underlying transaction.
Cross-currency swaps permitted only for SAFE-registered external debt from the Taiwan parent, with an amortisation schedule matching the principal repayment profile of the loan.
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for the onshore WFOE; any NDF overlay must be executed by the Taiwan parent and confined to the parent's own currency exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Directors, Supervisors, Managers, and 1%+ Shareholders Disclosure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (MOEA/DOE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 every calendar year covering the prior calendar year; any change in reported persons must be filed within 15 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Article 22-1 of the Taiwan Company Act, failure to file or false filing subjects the responsible person to a fine of NT$50,000-500,000 (approximately US$1,590-15,870), plus an order to rectify; continued noncompliance results in successive fines until corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (local tax collection authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 through May 31 following the close of each taxable year; special fiscal-year filers must file within five months after the fiscal year-end; electronic filing extension may apply as announced by the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or understatement triggers penalty up to 3 times the underpaid tax (minimum NT$1,500 for non-taxable filings); late payment attracts a surcharge of 1% for every two days of delay, capped at 15%, plus default interest; enforced collection may be initiated after 30 days.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Business Report (filed for recordation with the central authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of each fiscal year, i.e., June 30 for calendar-year companies; extension may be granted upon legitimate application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Article 20 of the Taiwan Company Act, the responsible person may be fined NT$10,000-50,000 (approximately US$320-1,590); if not corrected within the prescribed deadline, successive fines of NT$20,000-100,000 (approximately US$640-3,180) per breach are imposed until rectification; the company may also be denied subsequent registration approvals.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 20 of the Taiwan Company Act and the MOEA certification rules, an independent CPA audit is statutorily mandatory when the company's paid-in capital exceeds NT$30,000,000 (approximately US$950,000). This is the sole general corporate threshold; there are no separate statutory audit triggers based solely on turnover or employee headcount for a standard BPO call-center WFOE. Publicly-listed/OTC companies and regulated financial institutions are subject to additional mandatory audit regimes; if a non-listed company applies for bank credit, tax loss carryforwards, or certain subsidies, an audited report may be contractually or administratively required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public limited companies in Taiwan must prepare financial statements in accordance with the Business Entity Accounting Act and the Business Entity Accounting Handling Standards (Taiwan SME GAAP / Local GAAP), with the option to voluntarily adopt Taiwan-issued IFRS (TIFRS). Public companies are strictly subject to TIFRS as approved by the Financial Supervisory Commission.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1 mandates that every non-public company file an annual beneficial-ownership declaration before March 31 each year, identifying all directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding 1% or more of the issued shares or capital contributions. Any reportable change arising from shareholding transfers or manager appointments must be filed with the MOEA within 15 days of the change. The annual filing is submitted electronically through the MOEA commercial registration portal; no separate UBO register is required to be maintained on-site, but underlying records supporting the filing must be retained for at least 10 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Directors Meetings
